script.1:
1. 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Attention, Be-Stronger Gym members. I’m Jenny Smith, a gym manager here. I’d like to remind all members of an important rule that everyone must follow. Please remember to wear a clean pair of exercise shoes when using our gym. Wearing dirty shoes inside our gym brings in dirt. This can cause problems for our machines when it gets into the moving parts. Also, if dirt gets on the mats or equipment you use, it can affect your health. So, make sure that you wear a clean pair of exercise shoes when you use our gym.
This will keep everyone safe and healthy. Thank you for your cooperation.
script.2:
2. 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Grandpa, the news said lots of people went to the fireworks festival yesterday. I think fireworks are so amazing.
M: I know fireworks are pretty, but I’m not a fan of them.
W: Why not? Everybody likes fireworks.
M: Well, fireworks can be harmful to the environment.
W: What do you mean?
M: When fireworks explode, they can leave toxic chemicals behind, which might pollute the air, soil, and water.
W: That’s surprising. I’ve never thought they could hurt the environment.
M: Also, fireworks make big booming sounds and very bright flashes. This can panic birds nearby.
W: Oh, that could make them fly away from their nests, right?
M: Exactly. Like I said, fireworks can harm the environment.
W: Thank you for letting me know.
script.3:
3. 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Hello, viewers. I’m Dr. Sandra Frasier from the Everyday’s Tips channel.
Do you want to have strong interpersonal relationships with people around you? Here’s a tip. Sharing your personal stories builds strong interpersonal relationships. One of the possible reasons is that when you tell your personal stories to others, they feel like you trust them. In addition, once you tell your personal stories, there’s a high chance that others will feel safe and open up about themselves, too. By sharing these stories, you and others become closer, and this makes your bonds stronger. So, don’t forget that sharing your personal stories strengthens interpersonal relationships. I’ll be back with more tips tomorrow.
script.4:
4. 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
M: Ms. Robinson, what are you looking at?
W: I’m looking at a picture of the customer waiting room that I’ve just finished remodeling. Do you want to see it?
M: Sure. [Pause] It looks great. I like the two sofas.
W: I put them there for customers to watch TV while waiting.
M: Good idea. The star-shaped clock on the wall looks unique.
W: It does. I bought it from a local artist. What do you think about the stripe-patterned blinds?
M: I think they make the room cozy.
W: Yeah. I also put a bookshelf by the window. Customers can read to pass the time.
M: That’s nice. Look at the teapot on the table. It’s cute.
W: Thanks. I hope customers like the waiting room.
M: I’m sure they will.
script.5:
5. 대화를 듣고, 여자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
M: Clara, our school band club is volunteering at the community center for seniors tomorrow.
W: I’m excited to play music for them. As club leaders, let’s double-check everything’s ready.
M: Okay. I tested the sound equipment this morning. It all works.
W: Great. For the group singing, I printed out the words for the songs.
M: That’s good. What about the tambourines?
W: I packed them. The seniors will enjoy shaking them while singing.
M: They will. And the center will provide snacks for the seniors, so we don’t have to buy any snacks.
W: Excellent. Do we need to check anything else?
M: We need to get our club T-shirts from the school lobby. They were delivered earlier today.
W: No worries. I’ll do that.
M: Thanks! Then, everything’s set.
script.6:
6. 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
W: Welcome to the Grand Circus Museum. How may I help you?
M: Hi, I’d like to purchase admission tickets. How much are they?
W: They’re 10 dollars per person. The ticket price is the same for both children and adults.
M: That’s fine. I need five tickets for my family.
W: Sure. For your information, there’s a special exhibition on the history of Asian circuses. It costs 4 dollars per person to experience it.
M: Sounds interesting. I’ll take five special exhibition tickets as well.
W: Okay. So, you want five admission tickets and five special exhibition tickets, right?
M: Correct. Can I use this discount coupon?
W: Let me see. [Pause] Yes, you get a 10 percent discount off your total purchase.
M: Great. Here’s my credit card.
script.7:
7. 대화를 듣고, 여자가 K-music Pop-up Market에 갈 수 없는 이유를 고르시오.
M: Hi, Maya. Where are you heading?
W: I’m on the way to the library to return some books.
M: Okay. Guess what? The K-music Pop-up Market will open this Saturday for one day only. Let’s go together.
W: I’m afraid I can’t go.
M: Really? Are you still working part-time on weekends?
W: No, I don’t work weekends anymore.
M: Well, I heard you have a debate competition next week. Are you preparing for it this Saturday?
W: I’m not. The competition has been delayed until next month.
M: Then, why can’t you go to the pop-up market?
W: Actually, I’m going camping with my family this weekend.
M: Oh, I see. I hope you have fun with your family.
script.8:
8. 대화를 듣고, Open Buildings Week에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
M: Jane, did you hear about Open Buildings Week? Our city is opening some historic and well-known buildings to the public.
W: Interesting! When is it?
M: The event runs from December 14th to December 20th. But we need to register in advance.
W: Okay. How can I register for it?
M: You need to fill out and submit a registration form on the city website.
W: All right. Is there a participation fee?
M: Yes. For 2 dollars, anyone can explore the buildings. I have more information on my phone. Take a look.
W: Oh, there’s a special lecture about our city’s architectural history, too.
M: Isn’t that fantastic? How about going to the event together?
W: Sounds great.
script.9:
9. Hanbok Day에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
M: Hello, students! I’m Vice Principal Minsu Kim. I’m excited to announce the upcoming Hanbok Day event at our school! This event will be held next Friday. On that day, you’ll have the opportunity to participate in traditional Korean cultural activities, like games and dances. Also, you can learn about how Hanboks are designed. Students are encouraged to come to school dressed in a Hanbok. If you don’t own a Hanbok, our school will lend you one. However, Hanbok accessories, such as hats or bags, are not provided.
Lastly, to remember this special event, there will be a Hanbok photo zone in the art room. For more information, visit our school website.
script.10:
10. 다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 남자가 주문할 연을 고르시오.
W: Honey, what are you doing on your computer?
M: I’m shopping for a kite for our son Liam.
W: Do you want me to help you choose one?
M: Sure. Here are the five most popular models.
W: Let me see. [Pause] I think the 30-inch kite would be too small.
M: So do I. Then, what about the price?
W: Their prices seem reasonable except this one. I think 40 dollars is too much for a kite.
M: I agree. As for the shape, let’s skip the butterfly kite. Liam is not into butterflies.
W: You’re right. Now we have two options left. One has a kite tail, and the other doesn’t.
M: Let’s choose the one with a kite tail. It would look cool moving in the wind.
W: All right. Then, this is the kite for our son.
M: Great. I’ll order it now.

15. 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Amy가 Jake에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점] M: Jake owns a brunch café, and Amy works at his café. His café is doing okay, but not as well as he hoped, so he’s trying to find ways to increase sales.
Recently, Amy has noticed that more and more customers are asking for drinks that don’t contain sugar. She remembers an article that said many people are trying to cut down on the amount of sugar in their daily lives.
Amy thinks serving sugar-free drinks will increase sales by attracting customers who are concerned about their health. So, Amy wants to suggest to Jake that he introduce zero-sugar beverages to the menu. In this situation, what would Amy most likely say to Jake?

script.16:
[16～17] 다음을 듣고, 물음에 답하시오.
W: Hello, class. Some common stuff in our lives had different values centuries ago. Today, we’re learning about everyday objects in these days that previously demonstrated the high status of their owners. First, board games weren’t just a form of entertainment in the past. In Egypt, board games were expensive gifts to signify status. Some were so precious that they were even buried with royalty. Second, unlike today, ice cream was once only available for people with wealth and power. Making ice cream in warm regions required salt and ice, which were rare in the past. But people with power could access these resources. Third, mirrors used to be a main feature of the homes of the powerful.
Since producing them needed expensive materials and specialized skills, only those with high status could possess them. Lastly, tulips were once connected to a royal family in the Ottoman Empire. The royal family grew tulips and used them to display their power to foreign visitors of high status. Now, let’s watch a related video.
